subject: Spanska
title: Vocabulary: food and drink
sourceSummary: Words for food, drink, and meals, plus how to order and talk about what you like.

questions.opener: Not to be confused with "el pez", which is the live fish.
questions.explanation: "El pescado" is fish as food. "El pez" (plural: los peces) is used for the live fish.
"La cena" is dinner/the evening meal. "El desayuno" is breakfast, and "el almuerzo" or "la comida" is lunch.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "A mí me ___ las manzanas." (I like apples.)
questions.opener: Gustar conjugates based on the thing being liked, not the person doing the liking.
questions.explanation: "Gustar" conjugates based on the thing being liked: "las manzanas" is plural, so it's "me gustan". If the thing liked is singular, "gusta" is used instead, e.g. "me gusta el chocolate".

questions.prompt: How do you ask a friend "do you like vegetables?"
questions.opener: Swap "me" for the right pronoun for "you".
questions.explanation: For "you", "te" is used: "¿Te gustan las verduras?". "Me" is for "I", and "le" is for "he/she".

questions.prompt: You're at a restaurant. How do you politely order a glass of water?
questions.opener: "Quisiera" is a polite form of "I would like".
choices: Quisiera un vaso de agua, por favor.
questions.explanation: "Quisiera un vaso de agua, por favor" (I would like a glass of water, please) is the most polite form. "Dame agua" (give me water) is more direct/impolite.

questions.opener: A common word across all three meals.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "A mi hermano le gustan el arroz." (My brother likes rice.)
questions.opener: Check whether "el arroz" is singular or plural.
questions.answer: A mi hermano le gusta el arroz.
steps: "El arroz" (rice) is singular, so the verb should be "gusta", not "gustan".
"Le" is already correct — it refers to "mi hermano" (him).
The full sentence: "A mi hermano le gusta el arroz." (My brother likes rice.)

questions.prompt: Which food, drink, meal words, and gustar constructions should you know at the grade 8 level?
questions.opener: Food, meals, and how to express what you like.
questions.answer: Food: el pan = bread · el arroz = rice · la carne = meat · el pescado = fish · las verduras = vegetables · la fruta = fruit · el agua = water · la leche = milk. Meals: el desayuno = breakfast · el almuerzo/la comida = lunch · la cena = dinner. Gustar: me/te/le/nos/os/les gusta (singular) / gustan (plural) — the verb conjugates based on the thing being liked, not the person doing the liking. Ordering politely: Quisiera... = I would like... · ..., por favor = ..., please.
